 JUDGMENT
The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

Brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:
2.

That on 05.10.2019 at about 11-00 p.m. the petitioner was proceeding as a pedestrian on the left side of NH-75 Service road, from Mayura Hotel side towards Bellur Cross, Bellur, Nagamangala Taluk, Mandya District, at that time, rider of Bajaj Pulsar motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-54/K-9787 rode the same in a rash and negligent manner, came from behind and dashed against the petitioner.
Due to 3 SCCH-18 MVC No.6985/2019 impact the petitioner fell down & sustained grievous injuries.

3. It is further stated that, immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Adichunchanagiri Hospital, B.G.Nagar, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and undergone surgery and spent more than Rs.3,00,000/- towards transportation,
treatment, medicines, conveyance etc.,
4.
It is stated that, prior to the accident the petitioner was hale and healthy and he was Employee in Water Service Station, Bellur and earning Rs.15,000/- p.m.
Due to accidental injuries, he could not able to do his work as earlier.
5. It is stated that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of rider of the Pulsar motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-54/K-9787.
Hence the Bellur Police have filed charge sheet against the rider of said vehicle in Cr.No.183/2019 for the offence punishable U/sec.279, 337 & 304(A) of IPC.
As such, the respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner has filed the instant petition, seeking compensation.
After service of summons, respondent No.1 & 2 were appeared through their respective counsel, but inspite of sufficient time granted to the respondent No.1, he did not file his w ritten statement.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 filed its written statement.

7. The respondent No.2 filed the written statement and admitted about the issuance of policy in respect of Pulsar motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-54/K-9787 and the liability of this respondent is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.

It is contended that, the rider of offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving Gopi vs Shivaraj.R on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26391840/
2 licence to ride the said vehicle as on the date of accident, hence there is a violation of terms and conditions of the insurance policy.

It is the defence of the respondent that,
in order to help the deceased Rohan family, the petitioner has lodged false complaint against one Papanna Gowda alleging that he was riding the offending vehicle as on the date of accident, but on thorough investigation, the police have filed abated charge sheet against deceased Rohan S., hence the entire claim petition deserves to be dismissed.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner.
Ultimately contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive 5 SCCH-18 MVC No.6985/2019 and exorbitant.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition with cost.

8. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the parties, this court has framed the following:
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in an accident that was occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Motor Cycle and Dost bearing registration KA-54-K-9787 on 5.10.2019 at about 11.00 P.M.
near Mayura Hotel, on NH-75 Service Road, Bellur Hobali, Nagamangala Taluk,
Mandya District?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for? If so, at what rate?

From whom?
3. What order or award?
9.
In order to substantiate his case, the petitioner got examined himself as PW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P16.
Apart from his evidence, placed the evidence of M.R.O of Adichunchanagiri Hospital, as PW2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P17 to Ex.P20.

Further examined M.R.O. of K.C. General Hospital,
Bengaluru as PW3 6 SCCH-18 MVC No.6985/2019 and got marked documents at Ex.P21 to Ex.P23.

In addition to their evidence, placed the evidence of Dr.Nagaraj B.N. as PW4 and got marked documents as Ex.P24 & Ex.P25.
10.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 examined its Manager as RW1 and got marked documents as Ex.R2 to Ex.R4.
During the course of cross-examination of PW2, one document marked as Ex.R1.

Further examined F.D.A. at R.T.O office,
Mandya viz., Sri.B.A. Radhakrishna examined as RW2 and marked one document as Ex.R5.
Further, respondent No.1 examined as RW3 and he had not marked any document on his behalf.
In addition to their evidence, police officer by name Sri.Rajendra K. examined as RW4 and got marked documents as Ex.R6 to Ex.R11.

Heard the argument of learned counsel for the petitioner.
The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 submitted the written arguments.
Perused the materials available on record.

My answer to the aforesaid issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative  Issue No.2: Partly in Affirmative  Issue No.3: As per final order  for the following:
 R E A S O N S  ISSUE No.1:-
13.

It is the specific case of the petitioner that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the Pulsar motor cycle bearing registration No.KA- 54-K-9787 the alleged accident had taken place, consequently he had sustained grievous injuries.

14. On the other hand, the respondent No.2 contended that, the petitioner has lodged false complaint against one Papanna Gowda alleging that he was riding the offending vehicle as on the date of accident, but on thorough investigation, the police have filed abated charge sheet against deceased Rohan S., as Rohan had no valid and effective driving licence, hence, implicated one Papanna Gowda as the rider of the offending vehicle as on the date of accident.
15.
The petitioner in order to prove his case, examined himself as PW1.
In his examination-in-chief 8 SCCH-18 MVC No.6985/2019 by way of affidavit, he has reiterated the averments made in the petition.
16. The petitioner in support of his oral evidence has relied upon police documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P7.
Ex. P1

- true copy of the F.I.R., Ex.P2-true copy of first information statement, Ex.P3-true copy of the spot mahazar, Ex.P4-true copy of spot sketch, Ex-P5-true copy of wound certificate,
Ex-P6-true copy of IMV report and Ex.P7-true copy of charge sheet
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has examined Manager of the insurance company as RW1.

He has deposed in his evidence that the petitioner had given false complaint on 6.10.2019 before the police stating that, one Papanna Gowda was the rider of the motor cycle by suppressing that the deceasd Rohan S., was the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-54-K- 9787 as on the date of accident.
The jurisdictional police after thorough investigation have filed abated charge sheet against the deceased stating that deceased Rohan was riding the vehicle as on the date of accident.

He has placed police copy, inquest mahazar, statement of Shivaraju as Ex.R2 to Ex.R4. 9 SCCH-18 MVC No.6985/2019 Gopi vs Shivaraj.R on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26391840/
4 18.

Nagamangala.
19. Apart from this, the respondent No.2 has examined respondent No.1 as RW3.

He has stated that,
he is the father of the deceased Rohan and police have filed charge sheet against his son.
On the date of accident one Papannagowda was riding the motor cycle and not his son.
In the hospital records, it is mentioned that, his son was riding the motor cycle, on account of demise of his son, he has not readover the contents and signed the documents.
This witness turned hostile and cross-examined the respondent No.2, in the cross- examination he has denied that, his son was riding the motor cycle as on the date of accident.
Further denied that, his son had no driving licence, hence, he has implicated his brother's son Papanna as rider.
20. Further, the respondent No.2 has examined ACP, Mysore city as RW4.
He has deposed in his evidence that, in the month of November 2019 to February 2021 he was working in Nagamangala police station.
He was investigated the case.
On 19.12.2019 he had issued notice u/s 133 of MV Act to the owner of the vehicle by name Shivaraju and received the reply to 10 SCCH-18 MVC No.6985/2019 the said notice on 9.2.2020.
Further stated that, he was recorded the statements of Gopi and eye witness Prashanth.
He has further deposed that on 29.2.2022 Papannagowda had not taken any treatment at Adichunchanagiri hospital.
On 3.3.2020 he took the statement from the petitioner and received IMV report and RFSL report and filed abated charges sheet.

At this stage,
this witness considered as hostile and cross- examined.
In his cross-examination, he has stated that FIR has been registered against one Papanna gowda as per the complaint.

After investigation charge sheet has been filed against Rohan S., for the reason that, his father Shivaraju stated in the inquest report that his son was riding the motor cycle, further surrounded villagers have stated that one Rohan S., was riding the motor cycle and eye witness Prashanth Kumar had stated that Rohan S.,
was riding the motor cycle.
He has placed notice u/s 133 of MV Act and its reply at Ex.R6 to Ex.R8.
Further placed statement of witnesses at Ex.R9 to Ex.R11.
21.Under these circumstances
, it is necessary to consider, who is the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-54-K-9787 as on the date of accident. 11 SCCH-18 MVC No.6985/2019 22.
Now, it is relevant to go through the documents placed before this court.
On perusal of Ex.P1-FIR reveals that on the basis of complaint at Ex.P2, the case has been registered against one Papannagowda,
On going through the Ex.P3-spot mahazar reveals that one Rohan was riding the motor cycle and dashed against the petitioner.
Ex.P4 sketch reveals the scene of occurrence.
Ex.P6-IMV report reveals that front side of the bike damaged and IMV inspector had opined that the accident was not due to any mechanical defects of the motor vehicle.

23. Ultimately on perusal of charge sheet clearly reflects that, after thorough investigation the I.O.
has filed charge sheet against Rohan S. for the offences punishable u/s 279, 337 and 304(A) of IPC.
24. Added to this, on perusal of Ex.R6 to Ex.R8 i.e., notice u/s 133 of MV act and its reply and form No.29 clearly reveals that one Rohan was the rider of the motor cycle at the time of accident.

Apart from this, on perusal of Ex.R9 reveals that the police have written letter to S.C. Giri Hospital, BG Gopi vs Shivaraj.R on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26391840/
5 Nagar, to furnish information regarding the injuries sustained by Papannagowda in the alleged accident and the hospital 12 SCCH-18 MVC No.6985/2019 authorities have given reply that Papannagowda has not admitted to their hospital and not taken any treatment in their hospital.

sentences.text: Ex. P10
-statement of eye witness clearly discloses that due to the negligence act of the Rohan the accident was occurred and the petitioner had sustained injuries.

Ex.P11 is the further statement of the petitioner, clearly reveals that, he had already lodged false complaint against one Papannagowda, who was riding the motor cycle instead of mentioning Rohan S., in the accident.
25. Overall appreciation of evidence of RW1 & RW4, it is clear that one Rohan S. was riding the motor cycle as on the date of accident.

Even on perusal of evidence of RW2, who is the father of the Rohan S. and the respondent No.1 in this case, though he has examined, but his evidence will not support to prove that one Papannagowda was the rider of the motor cycle, due to his negligence the accident occurred and not from Rohan S.
Moreover, he is not an eye witness to the incident.
Though the learned counsel for the petitioner has cross-examined this witness, but nothing has been elicited from his mouth to prove that one Papannagowda was the rider of the motor cycle.
Even though, the complaint was lodged against 13 SCCH-18 MVC No.6985/2019 Papannagowda, who was riding the motor cycle, but after thorough investigation the I.O. has charge sheeted against Rohan S.

Even as per the say of respondent No.1, one Papannegowda was the rider and not Rohan, why he has not placed the evidence of Papannegowda to prove that he was riding the motor cycle as on the date of accident and he had not sustained any injuries and he had taken the petitioner to the hospital.
In the absence of the sufficient evidence and the documents, the contention of the respondent No.1 cannot be accepted.
26. Apart from this, PW1 was subjected for cross- examination at length, but no material answers culled out to believe the defenses of the respondent No.2 to disprove the case of the petitioner.
27. No doubt, the accident and the injuries sustained by the petitioner is not disputed point in issue.

Hence, in the light of the discussion held above, it is crystal clear that, the alleged accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of rider of the motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-54-K-9787 by name Rohan S.
As such, the petitioner has placed the satisfactory and convincing evidence on record to prove the above issue.
Hence, without making much 14 SCCH-18 MVC No.6985/2019 discussion on the point of rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle, I am answering the issue No.1 in the Affirmative.

ISSUE No.2:
28.
This issue is with respect to the entitlement of reliefs claimed by the petitioner.

The petitioner through this petition, claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/-
on account of the injuries sustained by him in the accident under different heads.

29. Before appreciation of the evidence placed by the petitioner about the injuries sustained by him,
in the accident and its consequences, it is apt to note herein, the preposition laid down in the following land mark judgment, while appreciating the injuries cases in Motor Vehicle Act.

Gopi vs Shivaraj.R on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26391840/
6 Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India.
"In the aforesaid case, it was held that, the court has to make judicious attempt to award compensation to the loss suffered by the claimant.
The compensation should not be assessed conservatively.
On the other hand, compensation should also not be endeavouring to secure some 15 SCCH-18 MVC No.6985/2019 uniformity and consistency.
The object of awarding compensation is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done, as far as money can do so, in a fair reasonable and equitable manner."

"while determining quantum of compensation, in such cases, the court has to strike a balance between the inflated and unreasonable demands of a victim and the equally untenable claim of the opposite party saying that nothing is payable.
That sympathy for the victim does not, and should not, comes in the way of making a correct assessment.
But if a case is made out, and the court must not be chary of awarding adequate compensation.
PW1 has stated in his evidence that, he has sustained the injuries in a road traffic accident.
In connection with the injuries he has produced wound certificate marked as Ex.P5.

The said document discloses that, he had sustained the following injuries:-
1) Crush injury an front of lower part of left leg, fracture of tibia bone seen measuring 4x3 2) Tenderness over left knee joint X-ray left leg (left fibia) comminuted segmental fracture noted at mid shaft of left tibia and fracture distal end of fibula both bones frcture (tibia & fibula) left leg 16 SCCH-18 MVC No.6985/2019 31.
In connection with the above said injuries the doctor is of the opinion that, the injury No.1 is grievous in nature and the injury No.2 is simple in nature.

Further, the petitioner has produced discharge summaries issued by Spathagiri Hospital, Victoria Hospital & KC General Hospital as per Ex.P11 to Ex.P14, which reveals that petitioner was admitted to the said Hospital from 5.10.2019 to 6.11.2019, from 25.2.2022 to 11.3.2022, from 27.11.2019 to 8.3.2020 & from 24.12.2021 to 7.1.2022.
Apart from his evidence placed the evidence of MRO of Adichunchanagiri Hospital as PW2.
He has placed authorisation letter, MLC extact, police notice and entire case sheet at Ex.P17 to Ex.P20.
Further placed the evidnce of MRO of K.C.General Hospital, Bengaluru as PW3.
He has placed authorisation letter, inpatient record and x-ray at Ex.P21 to Ex.P23.
In addition to his evidence placed the evidence of Dr.Nagaraj B.N. as PW4.
He has deposed that the petitioner has sustained left leg type III compound comminuted both bones fracture at the distal 3rd & mid 3rd.
He has placed clinical note and x-ray as per Ex.P24 & Ex.P24.

On going through the discharge summary and mode of treatment given to him as fully narrated in the recitals of the above documents and the recitals of the case files 17 SCCH-18 MVC No.6985/2019 of the petitioner, clearly evident that, the petitioner could have suffered a lot of pain and sufferings, due to the injuries sustained in the road Gopi vs Shivaraj.R on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26391840/
7 traffic accident.
By taking into consideration of all these points, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.50,000/- under the head of Pain and Sufferings.

Loss of income during treatment period:
32.

PW1 has stated that, he was employee in Water Service Station, Bellur and earning Rs.15,000/-
per month.
In this regard, there is no iota of documents to show the income of the petitioner.

Hence,
in the absence of the documents, it is apt to take the notional income as per law.

On perusal of discharge summaries issued by Spathagiri Hospital, Victoria Hospital & KC General Hospital as per Ex.P11 to Ex.P14, which reveals that petitioner was admitted to the said Hospital from 5.10.2019 to 6.11.2019, from 25.2.2022 to 11.3.2022, from 27.11.2019 to 8.3.2020 & from 24.12.2021 to 7.1.2022.
During the period of treatment, definitely, there was some difficulty to his to do daily routine work and to do his work for livelihood at least for a period of five months by looking in to the nature of the injuries sustained by him.
Hence, I am of the view that, it is just and proper to award 18 SCCH-18 MVC No.6985/2019 compensation of Rs.70,000/- towards loss of income during the laid up period and rest period.

Medical Expeneses;
33.
The petitioner in connection with his treatment expenses, he has produced medical bills at Ex.P15 to the extent of Rs.1,41,007/- along with prescriptions at Ex.P16.
Except the suguestion there are no contra materials available on record to disprove the medical bills.
Hence, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.1,41,007/- towards medical expenses.

Attendant charges, food and nourishment and conveyance charges;
34.

The petitioner herein, as per the medical records and also on going through the discharge summary the petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient and as an outpatient, definitely the petitioner could have spent some amount towards, food, nourishment, conveyance, as well as attendant charges.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- towards attendant charges, food, nourishment and conveyance charges.
19 SCCH-18 MVC No.6985/2019 Loss of future income;
35 . The petitioner herein, asserting that, he had sustained permanent disability, consequent upon the injuries sustained by him.
In order to prove the same, the petitioner has relied on his evidence along with the wound certificate and other medical documents.

In the evidence of the PW1,
reiterated the same thing forthcoming in the main petition.
As already discussed above, wound certificate placed by him as per Ex.P6 goes to show that, he had sustained grievous injuries for which he took the treatment as an inpatient.
Apart from this, another material witness by name Dr.Nagaraj B.N. examined as PW4.
He has stated in his evidence that, the petitioner has sustained left leg type III compound comminuted both bone fracture at the distal 3rd and mid 3rd for Gopi vs Shivaraj.R

on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26391840/
8 whichthe petitioner underwent wound debridement and external fixator on 6.10.2019 and later discharged on 6.11.2019, again he got admitted to KC General Hospital on 27.11.2019 and underwent external fixxtor, removal and ilizarov fixation for the tibia and fibular osteotomy and later underwent bone marrow infiltration, later he got admitted to Victoria Hospital on 25.2.2022 and underwent realignment of the ilizarov fixator and discharged on 11.3.2022 and again admitted to Victoria 20 SCCH-18 MVC No.6985/2019 Hospital on 98.1.2023 and got his ring fixator removed and above knee slab was given.

In support of his evidence he has produced clinical notes and x-ray at Ex.P24 & Ex.P25.
36.

Further, PW3 has stated that, at the time of examination of the petitioner, he has unhealthy scar his left leg, walks with a walker severe wasting of the left lower limb muscles evidence of left foot drop.
X-ray shows left leg uniting fracture of left tibia.
He has assessed permanent physical disability of left lower limb at 79% and whole body disability is at 33%.
37. Over all appreciation of evidence of PW4 along with the entire medical documents the whole body disability expressed by PW4 as physical disability for limb is 79% and whole body is 33%.
Hence, by taking into consideration of point of disability expressed by PW3, it is apt to take whole body disability as 25% instead of 33%.
The same will meets the ends of justice.
38. In connection with the age of the petitioner is concerned, on going through the cause title of the petition reveals that, as on the date of the petition, his age was 25 years.

In support of the age proof,
he has 21 SCCH-18 MVC No.6985/2019 placed any Aadhar card at Ex.P10 for consideration.
On perusal of the said document, his year of birth is mentioned as 1994.
The alleged accident occurred on 5.10.2019.
Therefore, as on the date of accident, the age of the petitioner is considered as 25 years.
To the said age as per Sarla Verma case, multiplier '18' is to be taken into consideration.

39. Next factual aspect of the income of the petitioner is concerned, in his evidence the petitioner has stated that, prior to the accident he was workingatr Water Service Station at Bellur and getting an income of Rs.15,000/- per month.
In this regard, he has not placed any iota of documents.
In the absence of the material documents, notional income has to be taken into consideration.
But the said notional income is to be taken judiciously, by taking into consideration of the year of the accident.
It is pertinent to note that, in the case on hand, the alleged accident had taken place in the year 2019.
As per the notional income chart, I am of the view that, it is apt to take the notional income of the petitioner as Rs.14,000/- for the year 2019.

40. In the light of my detailed discussions held above, no doubt injuries sustained by the petitioner,
definitely come in the way of his future, in a slight 22 SCCH-18 MVC No.6985/2019 manner, to do his daily routine work, as well as to do his work for livelihood on going through his age criteria.

Hence, the petitioner herein, is entitled for compensation under loss of future income as follows:
Rs.14,000 X12 X 18 X 25/100= Rs.7,56,000/-.
Loss of amenities;
Gopi vs Shivaraj.

R on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26391840/
9 41.
PW1 has stated in his evidence that due to the accidental injuries, he is unable to walk, stand long time, limping while walking, not able to sit cross leg and not able to use Indian toilet.

On perusal of evidence of PW1 and PW4 and also medical documents, I am of the view that, the petitioner will suffer a slight problem in future also, to do his normal work, as well as his work for livelihood.
Hence, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.40,000/- towards loss of amenities.

Future Medical Expenses;
42.
PW4 has stated that petitioner needs more procedures for the union of left leg bones.
Either PW1 or PW4 have not placed any estimation in this regard.

On going through the injuries sustained by the petitioner and also escalation of rates in the medical field, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.20,000/- under the head of future medication.

In view of my discussions held above, on various aspects the petitioner is entitled for compensation in to to, under the following heads:
 Compensation heads Compensation  amount  1.Pain and Suffering Rs. 50,000-00 2.Loss of income during Rs. 70,000-00 laid-up period and rest period 3.

Medical expenses Rs.1,41,007-00 4. Attendant, Nourishment Rs.1,00,000-00 and Conveyance Charges 5. Loss of future income Rs.7,56,000-00 due to disability 6. Loss of Amenities Rs. 40,000-00 7.Future medical expenses Rs. 20,000-00 Total Rs.11,77,007-00 44.

Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.11,77,007/- (Rupees elevel lakhs seventy seven thousand and seven only), along with interest @ 6% per annum, as per the proposition laid down by the Honourable High court of Karnataka in, MFA No.103557/2016,
between Sri Ram General Insurance Company Limited V/S. Lakshmi And Others dated. 20.03.2018.

LIABILITY:

10 45.

As regards the liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioner that, due to actionable negligence on the part of the rider (Rohan S.) of the motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-54-K-9787 alleged accident had taken place.
The evidence given by the petitioner in connection with the issue No.1, remained unshaken.
46. The respondent No.2 has contended that the rider of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.
Thereby violated the terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
As such, insurance company is not liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
47. To substantiate the same, respondent No.2 has examined Manager of the insurance company as RW1.
He has reiterated the contents as averred in the written statement.
48. Further examined official of the RTO office, Mandya as RW2.
He has placed Ex.
R5. On perusal of 25 SCCH-18 MVC No.6985/2019 Ex.R5, it is mentioned that there is no mentioned in online that the Rohan, the rider of the offending vehicle had valid and effective driving licence.
49. In this regard, on going through the Ex.R7- reply to the notice u/s 133 of MV Act, there is no mention about the driving licence number and valid driving licence.
Though the respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle had examined as RW3.
But he has not placed driving licence of the rider of the motor cycle.
Hence, it is crystal clear that, there is a clear violation of the terms and conditions of the policy.
50. At this stage, it is relevant to note herein, the decisions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court laid down in the following cases.
1). 2004 (3) SCC 297 between National Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs.

Swaran Singh &
Others

In the aforesaid case, with due discussions the Hon'ble Apex Court came to the conclusion that, the insurer has satisfactorily proved its defence in accordance with the provision of Section 149(2) R/W Subsection 7, as interpreted by the court.
And the Tribunal can direct the insurer liable to be reimbursed by the insured for the compensation amount, which has been compared to pay to the third party under the award of the Tribunal.

In one word it is necessary to note that, through this authority,
